review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

7:1.sourceText: Καὶ συνάγονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καί τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων.
7:1.targetText: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus,

groups.note: πρὸς αὐτόν (to him) is rendered around Jesus.
The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name.

7:2.sourceText: καὶ ἰδόντες τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὅτι κοιναῖς χερσίν, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἀνίπτοις, ἐσθίουσιν τοὺς ἄρτους,—
7:2.targetText: and they saw some of His disciples eating with hands that were defiled—that is, unwashed.

groups.note: The adjective κοιναῖς (common, defiled) is rendered as the clause that were defiled.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "saw that they eat" as "saw ... eating"; ὅτι has no counterpart.
BSB leaves the object τοὺς ἄρτους (the loaves) untranslated.

7:3.sourceText: οἱ γὰρ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐὰν μὴ πυγμῇ νίψωνται τὰς χεῖρας οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, κρατοῦντες τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων,
7:3.targetText: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.

groups.note: γάρ introduces Mark's explanation and is rendered Now.
ἐὰν μή (unless) is rendered until: they do not eat until they wash.
πυγμῇ (literally "with a fist") is an obscure term for the manner of washing; BSB renders it ceremonially.
The article is rendered as the possessive their.

7:4.sourceText: καὶ ἀπ’ ἀγορᾶς ἐὰν μὴ ῥαντίσωνται οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἄλλα πολλά ἐστιν ἃ παρέλαβον κρατεῖν, βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων,—
7:4.targetText: And on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining.

groups.note: ἃ παρέλαβον (things which they received) is rendered traditions for them.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 reads ῥαντίσωνται ("they sprinkle themselves"); BSB's wash follows the reading βαπτίσωνται.
The καί between list items is represented by commas in BSB.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the action implied by ἀπ’ ἀγορᾶς (from the market).
BSB follows the reading βαπτίσωνται ("they wash"); N1904 has ῥαντίσωνται ("they sprinkle themselves").
English introduces the list; the Greek sets βαπτισμούς in apposition.
BSB follows the reading καὶ κλινῶν ("and couches"); N1904 lacks it.

7:5.sourceText: καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς Διὰ τί οὐ περιπατοῦσιν οἱ μαθηταί σου κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀλλὰ κοιναῖς χερσὶν ἐσθίουσιν τὸν ἄρτον;
7:5.targetText: So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus: “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name.
Διὰ τί (for what reason) is rendered Why.
The dative χερσίν supplies with.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the object τὸν ἄρτον (the bread) untranslated.

7:6.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν Ἡσαΐας περὶ ὑμῶν τῶν ὑποκριτῶν, ὡς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ, ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ·
7:6.targetText: Jesus answered them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written:  ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB names Jesus.
εἶπεν (said) is rendered answered.
The dative article is rendered with and the possessive their.
ἀπέχει (is distant) supplies are; far renders πόρρω.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὅτι introduces the quotation and is represented by the colon and quotation marks.

7:7.sourceText: μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με, διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων·
7:7.targetText: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

7:8.sourceText: ἀφέντες τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ κρατεῖτε τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
7:8.targetText: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men.”

groups.note: The participle ἀφέντες (having left aside) is rendered as the main verb.
The finite κρατεῖτε (you hold) is rendered as the purpose phrase to keep.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:9.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Καλῶς ἀθετεῖτε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἵνα τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν τηρήσητε.
7:9.targetText: He went on to say, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.

groups.note: The imperfect ἔλεγεν (he was saying) is rendered went on to say.
Καλῶς (well) is ironic here and is rendered neatly.
ἵνα with the subjunctive τηρήσητε (that you may keep) is rendered to maintain.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render the addressee αὐτοῖς (to them).
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:10.sourceText: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ εἶπεν Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου, καί Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω.
7:10.targetText: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’

groups.note: θανάτῳ τελευτάτω (let him die by death) is rendered must be put to death.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; πατέρα has none here.

7:11.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε Ἐὰν εἴπῃ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί Κορβᾶν, ὅ ἐστιν Δῶρον, ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς,
7:11.targetText: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is Corban’ (that is, a gift devoted to God),

groups.note: The dative article is rendered to and the possessive his.
ὃ ἐάν (whatever) together render Whatever.
ὠφεληθῇς (you might be benefited) is rendered you would have received.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the reported statement; the Greek quotes it directly.
English supplies the copula; the Greek gives Κορβᾶν as a bare declaration.
English explains Corban as a gift dedicated to God; Δῶρον alone means gift.

7:12.sourceText: οὐκέτι ἀφίετε αὐτὸν οὐδὲν ποιῆσαι τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί,
7:12.targetText: he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.

groups.note: BSB turns ἀφίετε (you permit) into a passive.
The object αὐτόν (him) becomes the subject he of the English passive.
The dative article is rendered for and the possessive his.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:13.sourceText: ἀκυροῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ παραδόσει ὑμῶν ᾗ παρεδώκατε· καὶ παρόμοια τοιαῦτα πολλὰ ποιεῖτε.
7:13.targetText: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down. And you do so in many such matters.”

groups.note: The participle ἀκυροῦντες (nullifying) is rendered as a new sentence.
The dative article is rendered by the.
παρόμοια τοιαῦτα πολλά (many such similar things) is rendered so in many such matters.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ὑμῶν (your); you have handed down names the owners.
English leaves the relative ᾗ (which) unexpressed: the tradition you have handed down.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the preposition for BSB's recast; πολλά is the direct object of ποιεῖτε.

7:14.sourceText: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος πάλιν τὸν ὄχλον ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἀκούσατέ μου πάντες καὶ σύνετε.
7:14.targetText: Once again Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “All of you, listen to Me and understand:

groups.note: The middle προσκαλεσάμενος (calling to himself) supplies to Him.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render the addressee αὐτοῖς (to them).

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; προσκαλεσάμενος gives no name.
English joins the participle προσκαλεσάμενος to the main verb ἔλεγεν.

7:15.sourceText: οὐδέν ἐστιν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς αὐτὸν ὃ δύναται κοινῶσαι αὐτόν· ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
7:15.targetText: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him; but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.”

groups.note: εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς (entering into) is rendered that enters.
τὸν ἄνθρωπον (the man) is rendered him.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts "there is nothing ... which can defile" as "Nothing ... can defile"; ἐστιν has no counterpart.
BSB does not repeat αὐτόν (him); a man already names the person entered.
The relative ὃ (which) is absorbed in BSB's single clause Nothing that enters ... can defile.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English resumes the subject before are; the Greek has no demonstrative here.

7:17.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἶκον ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου, ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν παραβολήν.
7:17.targetText: After Jesus had left the crowd and gone into the house, His disciples inquired about the parable.

groups.note: ὅτε (when) is rendered After.
The aorist εἰσῆλθεν (he entered) is rendered had gone.
BSB renders ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου (away from the crowd) with the verb left: had left the crowd.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render the object αὐτόν (him).
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; εἰσῆλθεν gives it only in the verb ending.
English joins the two actions BSB draws from one Greek clause.

7:18.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε; οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἔξωθεν εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον οὐ δύναται αὐτὸν κοινῶσαι,
7:18.targetText: “Are you still so dull?” He asked. “Do you not understand? Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him,

groups.note: λέγει (he says) is rendered He asked.
καί (also, even) is rendered still.
πᾶν … οὐ (everything … not) is rendered Nothing.
τὸ … εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς (the thing entering into) is rendered that enters.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB puts the question first and leaves the connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render the addressee αὐτοῖς (to them).
BSB makes the ὅτι clause a separate sentence; ὅτι (that) has no counterpart.

7:19.sourceText: ὅτι οὐκ εἰσπορεύεται αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἀλλ’ εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν, καὶ εἰς τὸν ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκπορεύεται, καθαρίζων πάντα τὰ βρώματα;
7:19.targetText: because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated.” (Thus all foods are clean.)

groups.note: εἰσπορεύεται εἰς (enters into) also governs the second clause, where BSB supplies it goes.
εἰς τὸν ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκπορεύεται (goes out into the latrine) is rendered is eliminated.
The participle καθαρίζων (making clean) is rendered as the comment Thus … are clean.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:20.sourceText: ἔλεγεν δὲ ὅτι Τὸ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενον, ἐκεῖνο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
7:20.targetText: He continued: “What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.

groups.note: The imperfect ἔλεγεν (he was saying) is rendered He continued.
τὸν ἄνθρωπον (the man) is rendered him.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
ὅτι introduces the quotation and is represented by the quotation marks.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English cleft frame; the Greek says ἐκεῖνο κοινοῖ (that defiles).

7:21.sourceText: ἔσωθεν γὰρ ἐκ τῆς καρδίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἱ διαλογισμοὶ οἱ κακοὶ ἐκπορεύονται, πορνεῖαι, κλοπαί, φόνοι,
7:21.targetText: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery,

groups.note: N1904 begins 7:22 with μοιχεῖαι; BSB's verse division places adultery at the end of 7:21.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:22.sourceText: μοιχεῖαι, πλεονεξίαι, πονηρίαι, δόλος, ἀσέλγεια, ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός, βλασφημία, ὑπερηφανία, ἀφροσύνη·
7:22.targetText: greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.

groups.note: ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός (an evil eye) is an idiom for envy.

unmappedTarget.reason: English list coordinator; the Greek list has no καί.

sourceMoved.reason: μοιχεῖαι is rendered adultery at the end of BSB 7:21.

7:23.sourceText: πάντα ταῦτα τὰ πονηρὰ ἔσωθεν ἐκπορεύεται καὶ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον.
7:23.targetText: All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.”

groups.note: κοινοῖ (it defiles) gives its subject only in the verb ending, which BSB renders these.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English cleft frame; the Greek has only κοινοῖ (defiles).

7:24.sourceText: Ἐκεῖθεν δὲ ἀναστὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Τύρου. Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς οἰκίαν οὐδένα ἤθελεν γνῶναι, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνάσθη λαθεῖν·
7:24.targetText: Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre. Not wanting anyone to know He was there, He entered a house, but was unable to escape their notice.

groups.note: Ἐκεῖθεν (from there) is rendered that place, the object of left.
ἀναστάς (having arisen, set out) is rendered left.
εἰσελθὼν εἰς (having entered into) is rendered He entered.
οὐδένα (no one) is rendered Not … anyone.
The finite ἤθελεν (he wanted) is rendered with the participle wanting.
καί is adversative here and is rendered but.
οὐκ ἠδυνάσθη (he could not) is rendered was unable; ἠδυνάσθη is an alternative aorist form of δύναμαι.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence without rendering this καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; ἀναστάς gives no name.
English joins the participle ἀναστάς to the main verb ἀπῆλθεν.
English supplies what no one should know; γνῶναι has no object.

7:25.sourceText: ἀλλ’ εὐθὺς ἀκούσασα γυνὴ περὶ αὐτοῦ, ἧς εἶχεν τὸ θυγάτριον αὐτῆς πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον, ἐλθοῦσα προσέπεσεν πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ·
7:25.targetText: Instead, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit soon heard about Jesus, and she came and fell at His feet.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ (him) is rendered by the name.
ἧς … αὐτῆς (of whom … her) is a resumptive construction rendered whose.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐλθοῦσα to the clause before it.
English joins the participle ἐλθοῦσα to the main verb προσέπεσεν.

7:26.sourceText: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἦν Ἑλληνίς, Συροφοινίκισσα τῷ γένει· καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτὸν ἵνα τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐκβάλῃ ἐκ τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς.
7:26.targetText: Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin, and she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.

groups.note: ἡ γυνή (the woman) is rendered she.
Ἑλληνίς means a Greek (Gentile) woman.
The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name.
ἵνα with the subjunctive ἐκβάλῃ (that he would cast out) is rendered to drive.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:27.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτῇ Ἄφες πρῶτον χορτασθῆναι τὰ τέκνα· οὐ γάρ ἐστιν καλόν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ τοῖς κυναρίοις βαλεῖν.
7:27.targetText: “First let the children have their fill,” He said. “For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB puts the quotation first and leaves the connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render the addressee αὐτῇ (to her).
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats the object for toss; the Greek states τὸν ἄρτον once for both verbs.

7:28.sourceText: ἡ δὲ ἀπεκρίθη καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ναί, Κύριε· καὶ τὰ κυνάρια ὑποκάτω τῆς τραπέζης ἐσθίουσιν ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν παιδίων.
7:28.targetText: “Yes, Lord,” she replied, “even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

groups.note: In ἡ δέ the article serves as the pronoun she.
ἀπεκρίθη καὶ λέγει (answered and said) is condensed to replied.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
BSB does not render the addressee αὐτῷ (to him).
BSB leaves the partitive ἀπό (from, some of) unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:29.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Διὰ τοῦτον τὸν λόγον ὕπαγε, ἐξελήλυθεν ἐκ τῆς θυγατρός σου τὸ δαιμόνιον.
7:29.targetText: Then Jesus told her, “Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”

groups.note: λόγον (word, saying) is rendered answer.
ἐξελήλυθεν ἐκ (has gone out of) is rendered has left.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; εἶπεν gives it only in the verb ending.

7:30.sourceText: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσα εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς εὗρεν τὸ παιδίον βεβλημένον ἐπὶ τὴν κλίνην καὶ τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐξεληλυθός.
7:30.targetText: And she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone.

groups.note: εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς (to her house) is rendered home.
The article is rendered as the possessive her.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀπελθοῦσα to the main verb εὗρεν.

7:31.sourceText: Καὶ πάλιν ἐξελθὼν ἐκ τῶν ὁρίων Τύρου ἦλθεν διὰ Σιδῶνος εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ὁρίων Δεκαπόλεως.
7:31.targetText: Then Jesus left the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.

groups.note: ἐξελθὼν ἐκ (having gone out of) is rendered left.
ἀνὰ μέσον (through the midst of) is rendered into.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πάλιν (again) untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; ἐξελθών gives no name.
English joins the participle ἐξελθών to the main verb ἦλθεν.
English coordinator; the Greek has no καί before ἀνὰ μέσον.

7:32.sourceText: Καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ κωφὸν καὶ μογιλάλον, καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιθῇ αὐτῷ τὴν χεῖρα.
7:32.targetText: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.

groups.note: The impersonal plural φέρουσιν (they bring) is rendered Some people brought.
The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered by the name.
ἵνα with the subjunctive ἐπιθῇ (that he would lay) is rendered to place.
The article is rendered as the possessive His.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.

7:33.sourceText: καὶ ἀπολαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου κατ’ ἰδίαν ἔβαλεν τοὺς δακτύλους αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ καὶ πτύσας ἥψατο τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ,
7:33.targetText: So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue.

groups.note: The middle ἀπολαβόμενος means taking aside.
κατ’ ἰδίαν (by oneself) is the idiom for privately.
αὐτοῦ (his) is rendered the man’s.
αὐτοῦ (his) is rendered the man’s.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; ἀπολαβόμενος gives no name.
English joins the participle ἀπολαβόμενος to the main verb ἔβαλεν.
English joins the participle πτύσας to the main verb ἥψατο.

7:34.sourceText: καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐστέναξεν, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἐφφαθά, ὅ ἐστιν Διανοίχθητι.
7:34.targetText: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, “Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).

groups.note: ἐστιν (is) is rendered means.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

7:35.sourceText: καὶ ἠνοίγησαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀκοαί, καὶ εὐθὺς ἐλύθη ὁ δεσμὸς τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὀρθῶς.
7:35.targetText: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly.

groups.note: αὐτοῦ (his) is rendered the man’s.
BSB moves εὐθύς to the start of the verse.
The imperfect ἐλάλει is rendered as inceptive began to speak.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB says his tongue was released and leaves the subject ὁ δεσμός (the bond) unexpressed.

7:36.sourceText: καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν· ὅσον δὲ αὐτοῖς διεστέλλετο, αὐτοὶ μᾶλλον περισσότερον ἐκήρυσσον.
7:36.targetText: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.

unmappedSource.reason: Opening Greek conjunction is not separately expressed at this English sentence opening.

7:37.sourceText: καὶ ὑπερπερισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες Καλῶς πάντα πεποίηκεν, καὶ τοὺς κωφοὺς ποιεῖ ἀκούειν καὶ ἀλάλους λαλεῖν.
7:37.targetText: The people were utterly astonished and said, “He has done all things well! He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”

groups.note: ὑπερπερισσῶς (beyond all measure) is rendered utterly.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the verse-opening connective καί untranslated.
